description:
Census measured on develop 4a05ae2be. Counts are scalar_box_allocs per 1000 steps, given as interp / run / build. Probes and CLIF dumps: scratchpad nml9/ and nml-probe/ of session ebbfffd8. The interpreter makes none of the boxes below, so each one is also a three-path parity gap.

Needless boxes, one fix site each:
1. `Kernel.elem/2`'s guard `index < tuple_size(tuple)` (lib/kernel.fz:1434), 0 / 1000 / 1000. `fz_tuple_size` returns a raw int, and `fz_box_int_for_any` boxes it only to feed `fz_value_cmp_raw_const`. A user guard `k < tuple_size(t)` boxes the same way. The fix belongs in how a guard compare of two raw ints is lowered, so a guard-only comparison never needs a ref.
2. `acc + elem(t, i)`, 0 / 1000 / 1000. `elem` returns `any`, so the add is `Kernel.+/2[int|float, any]`. It computes a raw int and returns the int|float union through the `return_lanes` trampoline, which boxes it. A user function returning `any` into `+` boxes the same way, and one returning a specialized value doesn't. The fix is either a lane return for a union, or a precise result for elem. This one needs a page before it's built.
3. `self()`, 0 / 1000 / 1000. `ExternTy::Opaque(PID)` is boxed at prim.rs:2238 (box_opaque_word -> fz_box_opaque_for_any). `fz_send` (ir_runtime.rs:445) then unboxes it straight away (fz_unbox_opaque). This one box is the whole of fz-sc8.167's "send then receive boxes on native, not interp". Options: a raw pid lane, or an immediate pid ref like `atom_ref_word`. Either is a representation decision.
4. A receive clause binding that the body never reads, e.g. `<<_x::32>> -> nil` or a guard-only `<<x::32>> when x >= 0 -> nil`, 0 / 1000 / 1000. Every `ReceiveClause.arguments` entry is extracted and stored as a ref word in the out-slot (receive.rs:~398-419 via `store_receive_value_ref`, receive.rs:363). The fix is to prune unread body parameters where the clause is built. Guards read subjects through the dispatch, not through the out-slot.

Necessary under the current representation (named, not fixed here):
- A receive binding the body does use, e.g. `<<x::32>> -> x`. Out-slots are ref words (`value_ref_offset`, receive.rs:345), and park.rs materializes them with `closure_capture_set_ref_word`. Removing this box needs a per-slot kind, a raw capture setter and a RawInt body parameter.
- An int message to `send`: the message is a standalone mailbox value.
- A raw int passed to a parameter the program itself makes polymorphic (int|float), via push_binding_as_abi_arg (fn_ctx.rs:977). fz-sc8.167 owns the case where only spec widening makes the parameter polymorphic.

Not sites (the earlier version of this ticket was wrong about these):
- Tuple construction: `stored_form` (fn_ctx.rs:291) stores a raw word plus a kind byte, so `{i, i}` and `{7, i}` box nothing.
- The literal 7: a Known scalar is stored raw.
- Negation: it takes the raw lane, and the prim.rs:1709 box is only the guard fallback for an un-narrowed operand.
- A plain int message: it arrives as an AnyRef.
- The return value of `send`.

Acceptance: each needless site, once fixed, is pinned by a fixture in block 01700-01719 showing scalar_box_allocs 0 on all three paths. Sites 1-4 have independent fixes, so they split into child tickets; the split is proposed to the user first.

comments.text: More evidence (fz-9e2 machine-code study, machine.md M12): send(self(), n) with an integer costs 1790 instructions against 1501 for a binary, because the integer is heap-boxed (box_int_for_any x4, 2 scalar_box allocations per send).

Folds into fz-9x7.44 ("Scalars without addresses", user approved 2026-11-20): site 1 goes with fz-9x7.44.5 + .44.8; site 2 is fz-nml.9.2 (closes against .44.8); site 3 done (nml.9.3); site 4's box goes in .44.8, its needless extraction split out to fz-nml.31; the necessary receive-binding box and int-message box go in .44.8 and .44.6. Closes when fz-9x7.44.8 merges.

title: Native code boxes no integer or pid whose consumer takes it raw
